transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what really pushed me to come in today is... I've just been having these reactions at work. I work at a front desk, and lately, every time a door slams, or even if someone just rolls a suitcase fast across the lobby, I just jump. It feels like it’s happening all over again. And then it takes me a good minute just to get my heart back down. It's just getting really hard to deal with.
Have you experienced or witnessed a frightening or traumatic event that these reactions remind you of?
Yeah, I have. Um, this has all been going on for about two weeks now... ever since a guest threatened me while I was working at the front desk.
Since the incident, have you been avoiding places, people, or situations that remind you of what happened?

Yeah, I have. Um, I’ve been taking the back hallway at work whenever I can. Just... walking past the spot in the lobby where it actually happened makes my chest tighten up, and I just want to get away from it. So it's just easier to avoid that area altogether.
How long ago did the threatening incident at work happen?
Like I mentioned a minute ago, it was about two weeks ago. Yeah, just about two weeks.
Since the incident, have you had moments when you felt detached from yourself or as though what was happening around you wasn’t real?
Yeah, I have. Sometimes when I’m back near the front desk, the lobby feels kind of distant and unreal for a few seconds. It's almost like I’m watching myself work instead of fully being there.
Besides the reactions you’ve described, what other changes or symptoms have you noticed since the incident?

Honestly, I can't really think of anything else. Um... what I've told you is pretty much it. Just avoiding the front area and getting that weird spaced-out feeling sometimes. I haven't really noticed any other big changes besides that.
Did the guest threaten you with death, serious injury, or sexual violence?

No, um... no, it wasn't anything like that. He didn't threaten to kill me or, you know, seriously injure me. And definitely nothing sexual. He was just really aggressive, yelling and slamming his hands on the counter, getting right up in my face. It really shook me up, but he didn't actually make those kinds of specific threats.
How much have these reactions interfered with your ability to do your job or manage your usual daily activities?

Well, I'm still showing up for work, but... it's definitely getting in the way a bit. My manager actually had to shorten a couple of my shifts recently. I'm just a lot slower at the reservation desk right now. And, to be honest, I keep finding excuses not to cross the lobby when guests need help out there. It's just... I'm trying to get through the day, but it's definitely making things harder than they used to be.
